know_how.title: Dress in layers, in every month
know_how.text: The city is cooler and windier than visitors expect, and the weather changes from one neighborhood to the next. Carry a jacket even on a sunny morning.

know_how.title: The seasons, roughly
know_how.text: June to August: fog and cool wind near the ocean, sunnier inland and in wine country. September and October: the warmest, clearest weeks of the year. November to March: the rainy season, with crisp clear days in between and the shortest daylight. April and May: mild, green hills and wildflowers.

know_how.title: Sunset times
know_how.text: Around 5 p.m. in December, 7:30 p.m. in April and September, and 8:30 p.m. in late June. Plan sunset walks and cruises around your dates.

know_how.title: Tipping
know_how.text: Restaurants with table service: 18 to 20% of the bill before tax. Check the bill first, since some places add a service charge or a small health surcharge. Taxis and ride apps: about 15 to 20%. Bartenders: about $1 to $2 a drink.

know_how.title: Sales tax
know_how.text: Prices on menus and shelves do not include tax; it is added at the till. The sales tax in San Francisco is 8.625%. Other Bay Area cities have their own rates.

know_how.title: Cards and cash
know_how.text: Cards and phone payments work almost everywhere, including buses, trains and ferries. Carry a little cash for small Chinatown bakeries, market stalls and tips.

know_how.title: Car break-ins
know_how.text: Leave nothing in a parked car, not a bag, not a jacket, not a charging cable, especially at viewpoints and near the wharf. Take luggage to your hotel before sightseeing.

know_how.title: Book these first
know_how.text: Alcatraz and Muir Woods both need reservations and both sell out, in every season. Book them before anything else.

know_how.title: Street sense
know_how.text: Like any big city, a few central blocks are rough, mainly parts of the Tenderloin and mid-Market near Civic Center. Stay on the busy streets there, especially after dark, or take a ride.

emergency_note: Pharmacies such as Walgreens and CVS are easy to find, and some are open late. For a lost passport, contact your country's consulate: many countries have one in San Francisco.
travel_notes: The Golden Gate Bridge is not gold. Its color is International Orange, chosen so the bridge would stand out in the fog.
If the fog hides the bridge in the morning, do a museum or a neighborhood first and come back in the afternoon.
The sun sets into the Pacific here. Lands End, Baker Beach and Ocean Beach all face it.
